terms.definition: The smallest repeating unit of a muscle fiber that actually shortens; thousands of sarcomeres in a row make up a myofibril.
The thin filament in a muscle cell that myosin grabs onto and pulls during contraction.
The thick filament with tiny arm-like heads that latch onto actin and pull it inward, using energy from ATP.
A charged particle released inside the muscle cell that uncovers the spots on actin where myosin can attach, switching contraction on.
The cell's energy molecule; myosin uses it to power each pulling motion and to release its grip afterward.
The point where a nerve cell meets a muscle fiber and passes along the signal to contract.
The repeated attach-pull-release motion of myosin heads gripping actin, over and over, during a contraction.
